title: Eight Clefs

expected.notes: One part (Melody), one staff, 16 bars of 4/4 in C major, 4 systems.  Each 2-bar segment uses one clef: treble (bars 1-2), bass (3-4), alto (5-6), tenor (7-8), soprano (9-10), treble-8vb (11-12), treble-8va (13-14), bass-8vb (15-16).  Two staff-position patterns alternate, so the same note-head positions recur under different clefs: every pitch is wrong if a clef is misread.  Clef changes at bars 3, 7, 11, 15 are mid-system (small clefs before the barline); those at bars 5, 9, 13 fall on a system start and are preceded by a courtesy clef at the end of the previous system.  The small "8" above/below the G and F clefs changes the octave of every following pitch.

title: Octave Signs

expected.notes: One part (Piano) with 2 staves (must not be split), C major, 12 bars of 4/4, 3 systems.  Brackets labelled 8va / 15ma above the right hand and 8vb below the left hand: 8va from bar 2 to the middle of bar 3, 15ma from beat 2 of bar 4 across the system break into bar 5 (C8), 8va in bars 6-7, 8va from beat 2 of bar 9 to bar 10; 8vb in bar 3, from bar 5 to bar 6 (A0) and from bar 10 to the middle of bar 11.  Notes under a bracket sound one (two) octaves away from where they are drawn; the truth holds sounding pitches.  Outside the brackets many notes use 1-3 ledger lines.

title: Ledger Lines and Octave Signs

expected.notes: One part (Melody), treble clef, C major, 12 bars of 2/4, 3 systems.  The same passages are written twice: with ledger lines (bars 1-2 up to C7 with up to 5 ledger lines; bars 5-6 down to C3 with up to 4 ledger lines below) and with an octave bracket (bars 3-4 under "8" above = 8va; bars 7-8 under "8" below = 8vb), so bars 1-2 = bars 3-4 and bars 5-6 = bars 7-8 in sounding pitch.  Bars 9-10 are under "15" (15ma) and sound up to C8.  This item uses LilyPond 2.24's default bracket text (plain "8" / "15"); the direction (above/below) distinguishes 8va from 8vb.
